record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Effect of phase transitions on QSO dynamics
record.original_question: When a quadratic stochastic operator is generated by a Gibbs measure associated with a Hamiltonian H on a continuous state space, and when the underlying statistical-mechanical system may undergo a phase transition because the Gibbs measure is non-unique, determine how the thermodynamic behavior, especially phase transitions, affects the trajectories and asymptotic dynamics of the corresponding QSO.

evidence.quote: More precisely, if E is continual set then one can associate the Gibbs measure µ by a Hamiltonian H (defined on E) and temperature T > 0 [37]. It is known that depending on the Hamiltonian and the values of the temperature the measure µ can be non unique. In this case there is a phase transition of the physical system with the Hamiltonian H.
Problem 16. (by N.N.Ganikhodjaev) How the thermodynamics (the phase transition) will effect to behavior of the trajectories of a QSO corresponding to a Gibbs measure of the Hamiltonian H?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a continuous (measurable) state space and let $H : E \times E \to \mathbb{R}$ be a Hamiltonian. For temperature $T > 0$, let $\mu = \mu_{H,T}$ be a Gibbs measure on $E$ associated with $H$ at temperature $T$ (so $\mu$ is a probability measure on $E$ satisfying the corresponding DLR equations for the formal density proportional to $\exp(-H/T)$). Using $\mu$ as a kernel, define the associated quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V$ acting on the space $S(E)$ of probability measures on $E$ by
$$ (V\lambda)(A) \;=\; \int_E \int_E P(x,y,A)\, d\lambda(x)\, d\lambda(y), \qquad A \subseteq E \text{ measurable}, $$
where the transition kernel $P(x,y,\cdot)$ is determined by the Gibbs measure $\mu$ in the standard way that generates a QSO from a Gibbs distribution. It is known that, depending on $H$ and $T$, the Gibbs measure $\mu$ may fail to be unique; the regime of non-uniqueness is the phase transition regime of the underlying statistical-mechanical system.

Problem. Determine how the thermodynamic behavior of the system $(H,T)$ — in particular the occurrence of a phase transition (non-uniqueness of $\mu$) versus its absence (uniqueness of $\mu$) — affects the trajectories $\{V^n \lambda\}_{n\ge 0}$ of the corresponding QSO and their asymptotic behavior as $n \to \infty$ (existence and structure of limit points, fixed points, ergodicity, regularity, multiplicity of attractors, etc.). Provide an explicit qualitative and, where possible, quantitative correspondence between phase transitions of $H$ and the dynamical features of $V$.
artifact.category_tag: Quadratic stochastic operators and Gibbs measures
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of how phase transitions of a Hamiltonian's Gibbs measure influence the dynamics of the associated QSO is a known open question raised by N.N. Ganikhodjaev. While related works (e.g., Ganikhodjaev–Rozikov on QSOs generated by Gibbs distributions, and studies of QSOs on lattice models like Rock-Paper-Scissors) explore special cases, no general resolution describing the effect of thermodynamic phase transitions on QSO trajectories appears in the literature. The problem remains open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing QSOs generated by Gibbs distributions and their dynamics, indicating ongoing research without a general theorem linking phase transitions to QSO trajectory behavior.
status_evidence.claim: General relationship between phase transitions of the Hamiltonian and asymptotics of the corresponding QSO is not established.

status_evidence.title: Rock-Paper-Scissors Lattice Model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a specific lattice model where Gibbs measures and associated QSO dynamics are analyzed in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases connecting Gibbs measure non-uniqueness to QSO dynamics have been treated.

status_evidence.title: F-quadratic stochastic operators
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces F-QSOs and shows existence of unique fixed points with exponential convergence in the considered subclass.
status_evidence.claim: Available trajectory results pertain to restrictive subclasses, not the general Gibbs-generated QSO setting with phase transitions.
